Due diligence and pricing of credit portfolios in Brazil

Anyone buying or selling a portfolio of non-performing claims in Brazil needs to know what is really in it. We review each lawsuit and each debtor to reach a price you can defend.

Have your claim assessed

Who it is for

  • Investors and funds buying Brazilian distressed debt
  • Banks, fintechs and credit funds preparing a portfolio sale
  • Companies that want to value their book of claims in litigation
  • Managers deciding where to focus recovery efforts

What we analyse

  • Procedural status of each case: stage, service, attachments, appeals and deadlines
  • Limitation, nullity and pending defence risks
  • Solvency and traceable assets of debtors and co-obligors
  • Existing collateral and how enforceable it is
  • Estimated recoverable value and time to recovery

Ranking and price

Each claim is ranked by likelihood and timing of recovery. The result shows where the portfolio’s value lies, which cases deserve immediate effort and which should be written off or sold.

For buyers, this informs the bid. For sellers, it makes it possible to split batches and negotiate on data rather than face value.

Deliverables

  • Spreadsheet with the analysis of every case and debtor
  • Executive report with the portfolio ranking and recovery estimate
  • Strategy and pricing recommendation

Other services

  • Purchase of judicial claims We buy your Brazilian court claim, judgment or enforceable debt and pay now, taking on the risk and the time of collection.
  • Contingency-fee recovery The claim stays yours. We trace assets, structure the collection with the attorneys on the case and are paid from what is actually recovered.
  • Asset tracing We locate property, companies, shareholdings, vehicles and receivables of debtors in Brazil, and identify asset concealment and fraud.
  • Debt recovery in Brazil For companies and investors outside Brazil: we trace the Brazilian debtor’s assets and coordinate collection with local attorneys.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a minimum portfolio size?

There is no strict minimum. We review anything from small batches to large portfolios, with scope and timing adjusted to volume.

Can Poursuite buy the portfolio after the review?

Yes. In some cases due diligence is the first step towards an offer for part or all of the portfolio.

How is portfolio data protected?

We sign a non-disclosure agreement before receiving the data and use it solely for the agreed analysis.
